correctness.rationale: Independently replayed from scratch in this audit (new code, not trusting candidate tables). F9=F3[t]/(t^2+1) arithmetic validated by PG(2,9) census: 91 points, 91 lines, 10 points per line. Conic C=[0,10,20,29,39,52,58,66,76,88] has 10 points with at most 2 per line (nondegenerate). Witness A=C union S, S=[11,27,53,62,72,79,90], has 17 distinct points; line-occupancy spectrum {0:19,1:12,2:22,3:38} sums to 91 with max 3 and incidence sum 170=17*10, confirming a (17,3)-arc. Direct enumeration of all 728 nonzero codewords of the 3x17 generator matrix gives raw weights {14:304,15:176,16:96,17:152} (projective {14:38,15:22,16:12,17:19}), so d=14=n-k-1 with k=3; 38 trisecants exist so dual distance is 3: NMDS, as claimed. Punctured 16-point sets (drop 90 or 11) give weights with d=13, confirming the [16,3,13] NMDS / (16,3)-arc corollary. Global maximality re-proved by a third independent branch-and-bound (capacity model c+s<=3 per line; caps {bisecant:1 x45, unisecant:2 x10, exterior:3 x36}) reaching optimum off-size 7 in 243711 nodes / 0.29 s with a different witness [1,2,14,23,54,64,87], agreeing with the two committed scripts (17424 and 24389 nodes). Stabilizer re-enumerated by frame transport over all 1848 ordered non-collinear 4-frames of A: 8 GL(3,9) matrices, 1 projective class (trivial PGL stabilizer), matching the committed stabilizer.json. DRAFT's F9-irreducibility sentence is correct (2 is not a square mod 3). The result is a machine-checked exhaustive proof (replayable in <1 s stdlib), not heuristic evidence; scoping to the conic-plus prescription and the disclosed non-claims (no general non-conic classification, no Fan/Wang/Xu vs Donmez matrix comparison, no LRC proof) are accurate.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp logic. Gap source Donmez/Akpinar/Pelen arXiv:2608.18192 constructs [q+6,3,q+3] for all odd q and [q+7,3,q+4] for odd q>=11, stating admissible parameters exist for no q<=9 *within its parametric family* (sixth point on a distinguished external line). The candidate's (16,3)- and (17,3)-arcs at q=9 lie explicitly outside that family, so there is no contradiction and no implication in either direction. Live arXiv API searches confirm the gap: '(n,3)-arc AND PG(2,9)' returns only Bartoli/Marcugini/Pambianco PG(2,16) packing (max 28/min 15), cubic-curve completeness to q<=81, Xu/Fan/Han [q+5] maximal-arc families, and Donmez itself; NMDS+weight+conic query returns only Donmez; no source records a conic-plus (16,3)- or (17,3)-arc in PG(2,9), a [16,3,13]/[17,3,14] NMDS over F9 with this enumerator, or a sharp off-conic bound of 7 at q=9. Nearest prior on PG(2,9) sets (Bartoli et al. arXiv:1312.2485 semiovals/blocking semiovals of size <17) concerns a different object class (tangency condition) and does not imply the claim. The bound-plus-witness-plus-enumerator-plus-trivial-stabilizer package is therefore new; the DRAFT honestly discloses that monomial-inequivalence against named families was not computed, so originality does not rest on that unproved comparison.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later. Dimension-3 NMDS codes equivalent to (n,3)-arcs with weight distributions and locality-2 LRC use form a recognized program (Xu/Fan/Han 2022; Fan/Wang/Xu; Donmez et al. 2026; Bartoli et al.). The candidate does not restate textbooks or substitute parameters: at the smallest order excluded from the newest infinite [q+7] theorem (q=9), where character-sum asymptotics give way, it decides the exception computationally and overshoots it -- conic-plus reaches q+8=17, with a certified sharp stop (no 8th off-conic point for the fixed conic, hence for any conic by PGL transitivity), an explicit 17-point witness, full trisecant spectrum, derived [17,3,14] enumerator (and [16,3,13] by puncturing), per-point trisecant profile, and trivial projective stabilizer. This is a citable finite boundary fact with reusable stdlib-only exhaustive-search plus independent-verifier audit template, not a tiny unmotivated gain or unexplained enumeration.

PGL(3,9) transitivity on nondegenerate conics (fixing one conic WLOG) is cited, not recomputed; standard theorem, low risk.
